snip.t: Without prophylaxis, the infant is at risk of vitamin K deficiency bleeding (VKDB), which may present with bleeding from the umbilicus, gastrointestinal tract, skin or, particularly dangerously, intracranial haemorrhage.
snip.s: Neonatology 1: Newborn Assessment and Essential Newborn Care

snip.t: Vitamin K deficiency secondary to prolonged oral broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy
Easy bruising, petechiae: Vitamin K deficiency — Reduced synthesis of clotting factors
Nutritional: Vitamin K deficiency (poor diet, broad‑spectrum antibiotics) — Reduces synthesis of factors II, VII, IX, X
Vitamin K deficiency → impaired γ‑carboxylation of factors II, VII, IX, X → prolonged PT > aPTT → bleeding.
Coagulopathy: Anticoagulant use, liver disease — Warfarin/DOAC excess, severe thrombocytopenia, vitamin K deficiency
Describe von Willebrand disease, haemophilia A and B, vitamin K deficiency bleeding, immune thrombocytopenia and DIC.
snip.s: Paediatric Coagulopathies: Haemostasis, Bleeding Disorders and Clinical Manageme
